verdict.rationale: SumUp's documented Cloud API lets a POS on any platform start a transaction over HTTPS and complete it on a Solo reader. The docs also cover triggering and managing payments on Solo or Go readers, pairing and naming multiple readers, simultaneous transactions, and a Virtual Solo for sandbox testing. That is the server-driven terminal checkout the story describes. Missing for 10: endpoint-level detail on reader transaction status and result handling in the evidence, and independent or hands-on corroboration of the Cloud API terminal flow.

support.subject: As a developer, I can build a custom point-of-sale checkout that drives the terminal from my backend through a documented server-driven API

citations.quote: The Cloud API lets you start a transaction from a Point of Sale (POS) running on any platform (Windows, iOS, Linux, Android, Web-based, etc.) capable of sending HTTPS requests and complete that transaction via a Solo reader.
Trigger and manage payments on Solo or Go readers via HTTPS requests.
Ability to process simultaneous transactions on multiple Solo card readers at once - No distance limitation between your POS device and the Solo card reader
Use Virtual Solo together with a sandbox merchant account to test the pairing and checkout flow first, then switch to a physical reader later
